messages:
sophia: Heads-up — after rolling CNI v1.25 to west2-gpu canary, we're seeing readiness/liveness probe timeouts and a spike in p99 east-west latency. A few GPU pods restarted. Anyone else seeing this?

kai: seeing same. p50 fine but p99 tails blown out. suspecting encap path rewrite changes in the eBPF datapath.

miguel: tcpdump on affected node shows repeated SYN retransmits and delayed SYN-ACKs. ECN bits present on SYNs, then retransmit storm. example: 
```
14:32:01.123456 IP 10.4.0.12.443 > 10.4.1.45.55312: Flags [P.], seq 1:128, ack 1, win 4096, length 127
14:32:01.223456 IP 10.4.1.45.55312 > 10.4.0.12.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,nop,wscale 7,ecn], length 0
14:32:01.423789 IP 10.4.1.45.55312 > 10.4.0.12.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0 (retrans)
```

netops: confirmed on net metrics: PMTU probes + ICMP fragmentation errors increased post-upgrade on the east-west overlay. MTU negotiation is landing at 1452 on some racks, 1500 elsewhere.

ira: we're also seeing k8s readiness probes time out (tcp check) causing kubelet to restart containers -> autoscaler drains. Not a user traffic-wide outage but noisy for GPU infra.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT: high-latency-eastwest detected in west2-gpu (alert: net.p99 > 150ms for 5m). Pagerfired to @netops @kai.

kai: quick repro command I ran: 
```
kubectl -n ml debug pod/runner -- tcpdump -i any 'tcp[tcpflags] & tcp-syn != 0' -c 200
```
Captured SYNs with ECN and immediate retransmits.

miguel: hypothesis: the new eBPF encap-rewrite path in CNI 1.25 mishandles ECN/DF interactions causing PMTU blackholes when intermediate devices drop large frames. Combined with our tunnel overhead on some racks -> packets get fragmented or dropped.

sophia: can we toggle CNI config to disable encap-rewrite or fall back to iptables nat path? Any quick mitigations before rollback?

netops: two options: 1) flip encap mode to noEncap for the GPU node pool (needs node restart), 2) set node MTU+/traffic shaping to 1452 cluster-wide (smoother but disruptive). I'm drafting a runbook.

ira: suggestion: canary rollback of CNI to 1.24 on 10% of GPU nodes and monitor. That avoids cluster-wide MTU churn.

deploy-bot: started rollout block: paused further CNI 1.25 canary promotions.

kai: I've pushed a temporary iptables fallback flag on the CNI daemonset on west2-canary to force legacy path. early signs: reduced retransmits on that node after ~30s.

miguel: logs from the CNI pod show this error repeatedly around the time of issues: 
```
level=warn msg="encap rewrite failed: write to netlink: message too long"
level=error msg="failed to program encap rewrite for endpoint"
```

netops: filing internal ticket INFRA-NET-3421 with capture and suggested mitigations.

sophia: plan agreed: 1) pause canary (done), 2) rollback to 1.24 on affected pools asap for stability, 3) netops to validate MTU/encap config and propose non-disruptive fix for encap-rewrite, 4) postmortem after.

oncall-bot: NOTE: postmortem template created: https://redwood.internal/ops/postmortems/INFRA-NET-3421 (auto).

ira: will run rollback playbook now on west2-gpu canary set and watch autoscaler for churn; ping when stable.

kai: after iptables fallback test, readiness probes recovered on the node within 45s. putting metrics on the dashboard. :thumbsup:

miguel: leaving capture files in /mnt/tmp/encap-repro-2167894321.pcap for netops.

sophia: thanks all — prioritizing this for immediate rollback and follow-up.
